unis.name: Aberystwyth University

settingEvidence.evidence: The University's main teaching campus, Penglais is located on Penglais Hill overlooking the town and Seafront.

fees.text: £9,790 per year for Home (UK) undergraduate students (the current 2026/27 fee, set at the Welsh Government maximum regulated fee; Home fee status covers students from the UK). Aberystwyth says this could change for 2027 entry, so the 2027/28 fee is not confirmed yet.

source.evidence: The current tuition fee for undergraduate Home students is £9,790/year. This could change for 2027 entry and current students and applicants will be informed as above.

livingCosts.text: University self-catered single rooms cost about £124–£216 a week in 2026/27 (£4,839–£8,629 a year on 39–40 week contracts), including energy, wifi, contents insurance and Sports Centre membership. Catered, Welsh-medium Pantycelyn is £229 a week for 33 weeks (includes a £2,226 meal allowance).

contextual.summary: Applicants who have been in care, are estranged from their parents, have caring responsibilities, live in a disadvantaged area, have refugee or asylum seeker status, or are the first in their immediate family to go to university may get an offer towards the lower end of the typical range.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to two grades, or up to 16 UCAS tariff points, lower than the typical entry requirement (an offer towards the lower end of the typical range).

criteria.detail: Are estranged from your parents
Have been in care
Have caring responsibilities
Live in a disadvantaged area (based on your home post code). The page doesn't say which area measure is used.

Take part in the Welsh Government's Seren Network: email admissions@aber.ac.uk so Aberystwyth can make sure you're considered for a contextual offer.

contextual.rulesText: Depending on your situation, you may receive an offer towards the lower end of the typical entry requirement range. Aberystwyth receives this information directly from UCAS, so contextual offers are only available to applicants who apply through UCAS. Subject-specific requirements (for example a certain grade in a subject) still apply. The page doesn't say how many criteria you need to meet.

source.evidence: you may receive an offer towards the lower end of our typical entry requirement range (this can be up to two grades, or up to 16 UCAS tariff points lower than our typical entry requirement)

notes: Offers are published as UCAS tariff points with A level equivalents (for example 120-96 points = BBB-CCC), so every course is recorded as a tariff offer; applicants are selected on their own individual merits and offers can vary.

unis.name: Aston University

settingEvidence.evidence: Our campus is based in the centre of Birmingham, the youngest major city in Europe and a great place to live, work and study.

fees.text: £10,050 per year for UK (Home) students starting in 2027/28. Aston's course pages say this is expected and subject to parliamentary approval, and that fees will then rise each year in line with inflation (the 2028/29 fee is not published). The placement year is charged at £1,250 (a figure Aston gives for 2026 entry).

source.evidence: From 2027/8, tuition fees will be £10,050.

livingCosts.text: On-campus ensuite halls (run with Unite Students) cost £170 a week (7-bed flat) to £182 a week (5-bed flat) for September 2027 starters on 44-week contracts, with all bills (except a TV Licence) and Wi-Fi included. There is no deposit, but a £250 advance fee is deducted from your first rent payment.

source.evidence: Available for £170.00 per week, with 44-week contracts available.

openDays.text: Next undergraduate open day: Saturday 28 November 2026, 9am to 3pm (Aston's last of 2026). 2027 dates aren't announced yet. There is also an online Virtual Open Day.

source.evidence: Saturday 28th November 2026, 9:00am-3:00pm

contextual.summary: UK (Home) fee students from state schools who meet any one of Aston's criteria can get a lower 'Aston Ready' offer, assessed automatically when they apply.
contextual.typicalReduction: One or two grades lower than the standard offer (for example, ABB becomes BBB).

criteria.detail: Eligible for free school meals by the end of key stage 4, within the last 6 years (Aston gets this from UCAS' Modernised Contextual Data Service).
Live in a low participation neighbourhood: POLAR 4 quintile 1 or 2.
Declared a disability (Aston uses the information on your UCAS form).

Completed an Aston Pathways programme during Year 12 and 13 (email the Pathway Team with your UCAS number when you apply). Aston's Pathways to the Professions programmes cover Medicine, Healthcare and Engineering and Technology (STEM).
Studying at a school in the Aston University STEM Education Academy Trust: Aston University Engineering Academy, Aston University Maths School or Aston University Goldsmith's Institute.
Spent time in local authority care (declare that you are a care leaver on your UCAS form; your referee is normally expected to confirm).
Granted refugee status by the Home Office.

contextual.rulesText: To receive a contextual offer you must have attended a state school and be assessed as a Home student for fee purposes, and meet one of the listed criteria. Typically the Aston Ready offer is one or two grades lower than the standard offer. It is assessed at the point of application (no extra forms), except that Pathways completers must email the Pathway Team with their UCAS number. It does not apply to the Business and Social Sciences Foundation Year.

source.evidence: Our contextual offer scheme could reduce your undergraduate offer by one or two grades.

notes: All Aston course pages checked on 2026-10-21 show a September 2027 start and there are no 2028-entry pages yet (a September 2028 course URL returns 404), so every course uses 2027 entry.

Most Aston economics, finance and business degrees are 4-year courses with an integrated placement year. It is compulsory for UK (Home) students; international students can ask to opt out. Studying abroad is an alternative to a work placement.
Aston is not on UAT-UK's 2027-entry list of courses needing the TMUA or another UAT-UK test, and no Aston course page mentions an admissions test.

Foundation Programmes (A level entry CCC) exist for Economics (L10F), Business Economics (LN1F), Finance (N30F) and Accounting and Finance (N42F), and there is a Mathematics with Economics Foundation Programme. The first four also let you progress to other Aston Business School degrees (you still need the GCSE requirements).

Aston's Pathways to the Professions (Year 12 access programmes) are for Medicine, Healthcare and Engineering and Technology (STEM) only, so none is recorded as an Economics programme; completing one still counts as an Aston Ready contextual criterion. Schools can book KS5 Campus Experience Days that include Economics and Business subject tasters (not open to individual sign-up).
Aston is a compact single-site campus in the centre of Birmingham, with on-campus halls run with Unite Students.

contextual.summary: BU's AccessBU scheme can give you an offer at the standard tariff with a promise to accept you at least one grade lower (8 UCAS points), and in some cases lower still, if you meet its criteria or tell BU about your circumstances.
contextual.typicalReduction: At least one grade (8 UCAS tariff points) below the published tariff, and up to 16 points (two grades) in some cases

criteria.detail: You are care experienced (checked automatically when BU receives your application).
You live in an area of disadvantage: a postcode in IMD 2019 deciles 1-4 (England). BU also links to the equivalent lists for Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.
You are or have been eligible for Free School Meals during your secondary education (on the National Pupil Database).
You are from a British Armed Forces family: a parent or carer currently serves or has served in the UK Armed Forces, or you are a Service leaver yourself.
BU also uses UCAS' Multiple Equality Measure 1 to identify applicants least likely to go into higher education who are not in the categories above.
Estranged students can be considered through the AccessBU self-declaration form, with a reference from your school or college.
Students who care for close family members can be considered through the AccessBU self-declaration form.
Any other circumstances that have had a negative impact on your post-16 studies or GCSE performance can be explained on the AccessBU self-declaration form (the examples listed are not the only ones).

contextual.rulesText: BU automatically checks you against the listed categories when it receives your UCAS application, and falling into any one of them is enough to be assessed. You can also use the AccessBU self-declaration form (apply through UCAS first and give a reference from your school or college). Meeting a category does not guarantee an offer: BU weighs it with your predicted grades, personal statement, references and experience. All undergraduate degrees except Foundation Years are eligible.

source.evidence: an offer at our standard tariff with a commitment to accept you at least one grade below when you receive your results

notes: Every course here is offered in UCAS tariff points: 112–128 points (A-level grades BBC–ABB) from at least 2 A-levels or equivalent. BU says it typically makes an offer at the bottom of the range.
No A-level subjects are required (course pages say 'All subjects considered'); GCSE English (Language or Literature) and Maths at grade 4 are needed.
No admissions test: BU is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry, and the course pages say there are usually no interviews or selection activities.
AccessBU can lower an offer by at least one grade (8 UCAS points) and up to 16 points; it is discretionary, not automatic.
These courses are taught at Talbot Campus, Poole (Fern Barrow, BH12 5BB).

contextual.summary: Bristol makes contextual offers of up to two grades below the standard entry requirements to eligible home applicants who attended an aspiring state school or college, live in an IMD quintile 1 or 2 area, completed a Bristol widening participation programme, spent three months or more in care, or were eligible for free school meals.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to two grades below the standard entry requirements

criteria.detail: Attended an 'aspiring' state school or college, meaning one with low average attainment and low progression to higher education, as shown on Bristol's published lists of aspiring schools and colleges for the 2027 cycle (England and Wales, Scotland, Northern Ireland, Isle of Man)
Live in a home postcode in an IMD quintile 1 or 2 area (the 40% most deprived neighbourhoods), based on the home address on your UCAS form

Completed a University of Bristol widening participation programme: Access to Bristol, Discover Bristol, Insight into Bristol summer school, Next Step Bristol or Virtual Summer School (Bristol Scholars get a tailored offer rather than a contextual one)
Spent three months or more in local authority care
Been eligible for free school meals during your secondary education

contextual.rulesText: Contextual offers are only made to applicants with home fee status who are studying A-levels and/or the International Baccalaureate and apply through UCAS (not for CertHE Foundation or Gateway courses). You may be eligible if one of the listed statements applies to you; eligibility is worked out from your UCAS application and you are automatically considered.

source.evidence: Our contextual offer is a grade reduction of up to two grades below the standard entry requirements.

notes: All course facts are for September 2027 entry. Bristol hasn't published 2028-entry course pages yet (checked 2026-10-20: the 2028 address of the BSc Economics course page returned 'Not Found'), so check again before applying.

The BSc courses recorded here need A-level Mathematics. BA Economics (L150) and Politics, Philosophy and Economics (VL20) don't need A-level Maths but ask for grade 7 in GCSE Mathematics (the advanced numeracy requirement).

Study-abroad versions (4 years, own UCAS codes): Economics L105 (L101 with a modern language), Economics and Finance LN15, Economics and Accounting LN16, Economics and Management LN17, Economics and Politics LL14. Economics and Accounting with Professional Placement can't be applied for directly; students transfer from LN14.
Home students on a full-year study or work placement pay 15% of the full tuition fee and those on a whole-year industrial placement pay 20% (2026/27 figures).

Not added, to keep to 8 courses: Economics and Econometrics BSc (L140, A*AA including Mathematics), Economics and Data Science BSc (L1G1, A*AA including Mathematics), Philosophy and Economics BSc (VL51, AAA including Mathematics) and MSci Economics with Innovation.

EPQ: accepted to meet standard literacy conditions but not in place of an A-level. Core Maths isn't accepted in place of A-level Mathematics. General Studies, Global Perspectives and Critical Thinking aren't accepted as A-levels, and there is no preference for four A-levels or AS-levels.

Guaranteed offers are a separate scheme from contextual offers: applicants with a BS, BA1, BA2, BA3, BA5, BA14 or BA15 home postcode at a state school, Access to HE applicants, completers of Bristol widening participation programmes and applicants eligible for free school meals may be considered for one (https://www.bristol.ac.uk/study/undergraduate/entry-requirements-qualifications/guaranteed-offers/).
Bristol delivered its own Sutton Trust Summer School for the last time in 2024, so there's no current Sutton Trust offer at Bristol to record.

Bristol's own living-costs survey says undergraduates spent an average of £1,401 a month in 2025/26, including about £775.78 a month on rent or mortgage (https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/advice/set-up-finances/living-expenses/).

Bristol's 2027 admissions statements for the courses recorded here (PDFs linked from https://www.bristol.ac.uk/study/undergraduate/apply/admissions-statements/: Economics, Accounting and Finance, and Politics) say applications are scored on GCSE results (20%) and A-level results (80%), the personal statement is not normally considered (it may be used to separate applicants with the same academic score), and applicants are not routinely interviewed.

source.evidence: Cost per week: £179.97

source.evidence: Get ready to explore your future at an Undergraduate Open Day on 10 October or 21 November 2026 from 9.30am - 3.30pm.

contextual.summary: Home-fee applicants who meet any one of Brunel's contextual criteria are eligible for a reduced contextual offer (published on each course page), but an offer is not guaranteed.
contextual.typicalReduction: One grade lower at A level on the courses recorded here (ABB standard, BBB contextual), as published on each course page.

criteria.detail: Applicants from areas of low higher education participation (POLAR4 Quintiles 1 and 2), worked out from your Home postcode and flagged automatically on your application.
Applicants who receive or are eligible to receive Free School Meals (asked on the UCAS application; Brunel can sometimes access Free School Meal data provided by UCAS).
Care-experienced applicants / care leavers (asked on the UCAS application).
Young carer aged 25 or under at enrolment, with a dependent family member or friend (asked on the UCAS application under 'Caring responsibilities').
People estranged from their parents or carers (under 25 at enrolment): no contact with your parents or legal guardians because of a permanent breakdown in the relationship.
Refugees, people granted Humanitarian Protection, and asylum seekers (confirm your residency status on the UCAS application; evidence is requested later).
Students who attended the Brunel Urban Scholars programme (a Saturday programme for school pupils).

Also on the list: applicants with a disability; mature applicants (21 or over on 1 September of the year the course starts); people from Gypsy, Roma and Traveller communities; applicants from UK Armed Forces families (Service Children) and applicants who have served in the UK Armed Forces.

contextual.rulesText: You would be considered a contextual applicant if you meet one or more of the criteria. Contextual admissions only applies to applicants eligible for Home fees and does not guarantee an offer for your preferred course. Contextual offers are published alongside the standard offer on course pages. Essential criteria like subject requirements cannot normally be waived, and Brunel may ask for verification.

criteria.detail: Spent time in care (identified through information on the UCAS application).
Young carers (identified through information on the UCAS application).
Having parents/guardians who have not attended university (identified through information on the UCAS application).
Live in an area with low progression to Higher Education (POLAR score). The university considers applicants from POLAR4 quintiles 1 and 2.
Welsh, English, Scottish and Northern Irish Indexes of multiple deprivation (no threshold stated).
Attendance at a school with lower than average participation to Higher Education or those that have a higher number of students from low participation neighbourhoods.
Completed an accredited Widening Participation programme at Cardiff Met.
Applicants covered by the Armed Forces Covenant: those who serve or have served in the UK Armed Forces, whether Regular or Reserve, and their families and dependents.

Cardiff Met also uses UCAS Multiple Equality Measure (MEM) data, which combines sex, ethnic group, where you live (POLAR), school sector (state or private) and income background (free school meals) into one score.

Other personal circumstances that have negatively impacted your post 16 studies (for example disability, being estranged from your parents, or being a refugee or asylum seeker): tell Admissions at askadmissions@cardiffmet.ac.uk if you cannot meet the published entry requirements.

contextual.rulesText: If you are identified as meeting the specified criteria and are offered a place, you will receive an adjusted conditional offer, typically one grade (or the equivalent in points) below the published standard entry requirements. Course-specific conditions (for example a minimum grade in a subject) still apply. All courses are included, the policy only applies to applicants with Home fee status, and Cardiff Met can only use data supplied at the time of application.

source.evidence: you will receive an adjusted conditional offer. Typically, this will be one grade (or the equivalent in points) below the published standard entry requirements.

notes: All six courses are taught at the Llandaff Campus (Cardiff School of Management) and show Entry Year 2027; no 2028-entry pages were found on 2026-10-21, so 2027 entry is used.

GCSEs: five at grade C/4 or above including English Language (or Welsh First Language) and Mathematics (or Mathematics – Numeracy).
Cardiff Met is not on UAT-UK's TMUA list for 2027 entry and no course page names an admissions test.

Every degree also has a 4-year version with a foundation year (UCAS codes end in F; normally 32 UCAS tariff points from at least 1 A level or equivalent) and an optional year in industry between years 2 and 3.

criteria.detail: Care leaver or care experienced (e.g. lived in public care, foster care, kinship care or a residential children's home)
A parent or have parenting responsibilities (including pregnant, adopting, or a guardian or foster carer of a child)
Currently receiving, or received/eligible for, free school meals during secondary education
Have caring responsibilities (unpaid care for a family member or friend with an illness, disability, mental health condition or addiction)
Official refugee status in the UK, an asylum seeker, or limited leave to remain (also Ukraine scheme arrivals)
Estranged from both parents (not in contact with and supported by either of them)

Completed Cardiff's Confident Futures or Step Up to University (or Sutton Trust Medicine and Dentistry Summer Schools, Pathways to Engineering, Pathways to Law), or at another university Sutton Trust Pathways to Banking and Finance (including online), Engineering or Law; applying in the same year or the year after
POLAR4 (how likely young people in your area are to go to higher education): living in a low-participation area earns points towards your contextual score
Welsh, English, Scottish and Northern Irish indices of multiple deprivation for your home postcode: more deprived areas earn more points
DWP average household gross annual earnings for your home postcode: lower average earnings earn more points
Welsh and English sixth form performance data and free school meal rates for your school's postcode
Parents or guardians do not have a higher education qualification such as a degree (collected on the UCAS form)

contextual.rulesText: You are classed as contextual if you answer yes to any of the listed UCAS-form questions or complete one of the listed access activities. Otherwise Cardiff adds weighted points for area (POLAR4, deprivation indices, average household earnings), school (sixth form performance, free school meal rates) and parents without a degree into a score from 0-330: 0-99 is non-contextual and 100 or above signals disadvantage. Only information in the original UCAS application is used. Most applicants are not classed as contextual.

source.evidence: You will be classed as contextual if, on your UCAS application, you answer yes to any of the following questions ... be given an offer made at one or two grades lower than the standard offer

contextual.summary: UK applicants whose circumstances match Chichester's contextual factors may get an offer 16 UCAS tariff points lower (about two A-level grades); there is no separate form, you apply through UCAS as normal.
contextual.typicalReduction: 16 UCAS tariff points (equivalent to two A-level grades or one BTEC grade); 8 points for foundation year courses

criteria.detail: Having been in receipt of free school meals during your secondary education.
Living within POLAR4 quintile 1 (postcode areas with the lowest rates of participation in higher education).
Being a care leaver: having been in formal care for at least three months.
Having caring responsibilities: being an unpaid carer for a family member or a friend.
Having refugee status.
You or a parent/carer currently serve, or have served, in the UK Armed Forces.

Having declared a disability: a social or communication condition such as autism; blindness or serious visual impairment uncorrected by glasses; deafness or serious hearing impediment; a long-term or chronic health condition such as diabetes, epilepsy or cancer; a mental health condition such as depression, schizophrenia or anxiety disorder; or a physical impairment or mobility issues.

contextual.rulesText: Open to UK applicants applying for undergraduate courses. The page says these factors 'are considered when deciding if you are eligible' and does not say how many you need. Apply through UCAS as normal; Chichester may ask for evidence. If you are predicted two or more A-level grades better than the published typical offer you will normally be made the typical offer. Some courses with course-specific entry requirements may differ.

source.evidence: Our contextual offer is an entry requirement reduction of 16 UCAS tariff points (equivalent to two A-level grades or one BTEC grade) for all eligible undergraduate degree courses.

notes: Chichester doesn't appear to offer a standalone Economics degree: none is listed on its Business School or undergraduate course pages (checked 2026-10-21). The courses recorded are the closest matches (accounting and finance, fintech, business management).
Offers are in UCAS tariff points: 104 points (BCC at A level) for most courses; Fintech 104-120 points (BCC to BBB). The pages say individual offers may vary.

Business Management and Finance and Business Management and Marketing still show 2026/27 details (2026 entry) on 2026-10-21; Accounting and Finance, Business Management and Fintech show 2027/28 fees (2027 entry).

No admissions test is named on any course page, and Chichester is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry (https://uat-wp.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/01172717/Course_List_2027_Entry_Final.pdf).

Chichester's Outreach team offers talks, workshops and academic taster sessions (many for Year 12+, including Business School sessions) on request for schools and colleges; no application programme or summer school for individual students was found.
Business School courses are taught at the Bishop Otter campus in Chichester; the university's other campus is at Bognor Regis.
The accommodation page's detailed hall descriptions show older, lower prices than its 2026/27 comparison table; the table (which states 2026/27) was used.
Chichester's Halls vs Home page says all utility bills are included in the rent for university halls (https://www.chi.ac.uk/halls-vs-home/).

contextual.summary: Home-fee applicants to the first year of an undergraduate degree who meet one or more of City's contextual criteria can get a reduced offer, usually made automatically from your UCAS form.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to two grades (or up to 16 tariff points) below the standard entry requirements: one A-level grade lower with one criterion, no more than two grades with more than one criterion, and the full reduction if you have been in local authority care.

criteria.detail: Have spent three months or more in local authority care (taken from your UCAS form, so declare it).
Your postcode is in an area with low progression to higher education as measured by POLAR4: Quintile 1 or 2.

You attend a lower-performing school or college: in the lowest 20% for average QCA points per A-level student (or equivalent) in England, Wales or Northern Ireland, as identified by the Department for Education and provided via UCAS. City publishes a list of eligible schools.
You are the first generation of your family to go to university (information provided by UCAS).
Estranged student: aged 25 or below and studying without the support and approval of either parent because the relationship has broken down.
Have caring responsibilities: you give unpaid care to a family member, partner or friend who could not cope without your support.

Have received free school meals. City's wording: if you received free school meals up until the end of your final year, your UCAS application fee can be waived and the University may factor this in when making your offer (page refers to the 2025 cycle).

criteria.detail: You have a disability.
You are a care leaver.
You are aged over 21 at the start of your course.
You are a refugee or asylum seeker in the UK.
You are estranged from your parents.
You have long-term caring responsibilities for someone in your family.

You may also be eligible based on where you live: your home postcode is in an area where progression to higher education is lower than the national average (Coventry uses UCAS's Modernised Contextualised Data Service; no POLAR, IMD or quintile cut-off is published).
Pupils who take part in Coventry's Future Grads programme (chosen by partner schools) are given a Fair Access Offer.

contextual.rulesText: If you apply through UCAS for an undergraduate degree course, are a UK student and have declared any of the criteria, you will automatically be considered; there is no separate application. Eligibility is assessed from your UCAS application and UCAS contextual data (including whether your home postcode is in an area where fewer people progress to university than the national average). You must still meet the conditions of your offer and any specific course requirements.

source.evidence: Most eligible applicants receive a reduction of 16 UCAS tariff points from the standard entry requirements for their chosen course.

criteria.detail: Care experience: applicants who have been in care (listed together with estrangement).

Applicants with refugee status.

Applicants who are the first in their family to attend university.

contextual.rulesText: You may qualify if you meet one or more of the criteria. livingCosts.text: Edinburgh estimates about £1,546 a month for a single undergraduate in 2026/27: £13,914 for a 39-week academic year, or £18,552 for a full year. University halls average about £925 a month rent self-catered (range £414-£1,348) and £1,169 a month catered with two meals a day (range £842-£1,518), with utilities included, on 39-week leases.

contextual.summary: Edinburgh gives widening access offers: a 'Plus Flag' (normally an offer at the lower minimum entry requirements) or a 'Flag' (standard requirements, but you are prioritised where competition for places is high), based on your postcode, school, care/refugee/estranged/carer status and access programmes.
contextual.typicalReduction: Plus Flag applicants will normally be made an offer at the programme's minimum entry requirement (ABB for most of the Economics degrees recorded here, compared with a standard range of A*A*A* to A*AA); an offer is not guaranteed.

criteria.detail: Plus Flag: your home postcode is in the lowest Acorn quintile ('Acorn 6') and you attend a state school in England, Wales or Northern Ireland. (Flag, which keeps the standard offer but prioritises you: the second lowest Acorn quintile, 'Acorn 5', and a state school in England, Wales or Northern Ireland.)

Plus Flag: your home postcode is in the lowest POLAR quintile ('POLAR1') and you attend a state school in England, Wales or Northern Ireland. (Flag: the second lowest POLAR quintile, 'POLAR2', and a state school in England, Wales or Northern Ireland.)
Scotland only: your home postcode is in the lowest quintile of the Scottish Index of Multiple Deprivation ('SIMD20').

Scotland only: you attend one of Edinburgh's identified Scottish target schools (chosen for low progression to higher education, high free school meal entitlement and many SIMD20 postcodes) or a LEAPS Group 1 or Group 1 Plus school.
You are care experienced.
You are a refugee or an asylum seeker.
You are estranged from your parents or guardians and are under 25 at the start of your degree.
You are a carer and have completed one or more of Edinburgh's recognised bridging programmes.
You are undertaking a Scottish Wider Access Programme (SWAP) course or Edinburgh's own Access Programme (routes for college students and adult learners).

contextual.rulesText: You are eligible for a Plus Flag if you are permanently resident in the UK and fulfil one or more of the Plus Flag criteria. With a Plus Flag you will normally be made an offer at the minimum entry requirement, as long as you are predicted to meet it and have the required subjects; this is not guaranteed. A Flag (for example Acorn 5 or POLAR2 plus a state school in England, Wales or Northern Ireland) keeps the standard entry requirements but prioritises you for places on programmes where competition is high. Acorn and POLAR data are updated each May, so use Edinburgh's checker tool to see whether you qualify.

source.evidence: You are eligible for a Plus Flag if you're permanently resident in the UK and fulfil one or more of these criteria:

notes: Scottish university: the degrees recorded are 4-year MA (Hons) degrees. The A level offers are for students from the rest of the UK.

Edinburgh publishes the range of grades most applicants needed to receive an offer in recent years (for example A*A*A* to A*AA for Economics). The top of the range is recorded as the typical offer and the bottom as the low end.

Widening access: applicants assigned a Plus Flag are normally made an offer at the minimum entry requirement (ABB for most courses recorded here; A*BB including A* in Mathematics for Economics and Mathematics). This is recorded in each course's alternative offers.

Edinburgh is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry (https://uat-wp.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/01172717/Course_List_2027_Entry_Final.pdf) and no course page names an admissions test.

Psychology and Economics MA (Hons) (CZ81) says it is closed to new applications for 2027, so it was not recorded. Other Economics-related joint degrees not recorded because of the course limit: Economics and Statistics (LG13), Philosophy and Economics (VL51), Social Policy and Economics (LL41), Business with Strategic Economics (N1L1), Accounting and Finance (NN43) and Finance and Business (NN13).

criteria.detail: Students residing in the UK who are estranged from their parents.
Young carer: students residing in the UK who helped to look after someone in their family who is ill, disabled, has a mental health condition.
Military families: students residing in the UK who have a parent or carer serving in the Armed Forces.
Where residing in the UK, students with 'refugee status' or 'Humanitarian Protection', and asylum seekers.
Students residing in the UK, who are (or have been) eligible or receiving free school meals during their secondary education.
Students residing in the UK where there is low progression to Higher Education, defined as Quintiles 1 and 2 from OfS POLAR4 data.
Students residing in the UK who have experience of care, for example foster care, residential care, being looked after at home under a supervision order, or kinship care (officially or informally).
Disability: students residing in the UK who have declared one or more disability type on their application.

contextual.rulesText: Applicants who apply in the 2027 cycle may be made a contextual offer based on one of the listed criteria. You do not need to do anything: apply as normal and, if you are eligible, your offer letter will tell you. Contextual offers are available for most but not all courses (not for degrees with a foundation year, among others). Not eligible: second/final year entrants, recognised transfer programme applicants, applicants taking vocational or work-based learning qualifications, and applicants taking qualifications graded pass or fail. Your offer may still include specific subject or GCSE conditions.

contextual.summary: Exeter makes lower contextual offers (usually two grades below the typical offer, three for care-experienced applicants) to applicants who meet any one of its published criteria.
contextual.typicalReduction: Two-grade adjustment for most criteria; three-grade adjustment for care leavers and care-experienced applicants; up to three grades for progression-programme participants and refugees/asylum seekers

criteria.detail: Live in a low-participation area (POLAR4 quintile 1 or 2) and attend a state school — two grades
Live in a low-participation area (TUNDRA MSOA quintile 1 or 2) and attend a state school — two grades
Live in an area of deprivation (IMD quintile 1 or 2) and attend a state school — two grades

Attend a non-selective state school or college in the South West or Wales on Exeter's Contextual Offer Schools and Colleges List (PDF: https://www.exeter.ac.uk/v8media/recruitmentsites/documents/20278_UoE_Contextual_Offer_Schools_Colleges_List.pdf) — two grades
Have received free school meals and attend a state school — two grades
Applying from an Elephant Group school, completed the Bridges to HE programme, or did activity with an IntoUniversity centre in Years 10–13 — two grades
SEREN partnership (Wales) participants who completed a Seren Academic Challenge Series or the SEREN University of Exeter Residential — two grades
Care leaver or care experienced — three grades
Carer — two grades
Estranged student — two grades
Have parental responsibility — two grades

Registered on a progression programme run or managed by Exeter: Exeter Scholars, Realising Opportunities, Sutton Trust Pathways to Law (in person and online), Sutton Trust Pathways to Banking & Finance (online), Mature Access Pathway — up to three grades
Seeking asylum, limited leave to remain and from a state school, humanitarian protection, or refugee status — up to three grades

contextual.rulesText: You are eligible for a contextual offer if you meet one of the criteria; the application process is still competitive so an offer isn't guaranteed. Where courses have specific subject requirements, grade adjustments may differ, and GCSE requirements are not reduced.

source.evidence: You are eligible for a contextual offer at a lower grade than our typical entry requirements if you meet one of the criteria below

notes: All courses listed are taught at the Streatham Campus, Exeter (University of Exeter Business School).

BSc Economics and BSc Economics and Finance need A-level Maths at grade B; Business Economics, Economics and Politics, PPE, Accounting and Finance and Business and Management have no A-level subject requirement (GCSE Maths 5–7 instead).
Exeter gives up to a three-grade contextual adjustment to participants of Realising Opportunities, Sutton Trust Pathways to Law and Sutton Trust Pathways to Banking & Finance (online).
Exeter Scholars has three Year 12 routes: South West on-campus (Devon, Cornwall, Somerset, Bristol, Dorset), Virtual (UK-wide) and National residential (outside the South West).

Rent includes heating, utilities, Wi-Fi and contents insurance. Most contracts run from 11 September 2026 to 11 June 2027.

openDays.text: Next undergraduate open day: Saturday 24 October 2026, 9am to 3pm on the Glasgow campus. No later open days are listed yet.

source.evidence: Saturday 24 October, 9am - 3pm

contextual.summary: Glasgow's lower 'adjusted' offers are only for applicants living in Scotland. Students from England, Wales or Northern Ireland can only get a possible adjusted offer by completing Glasgow's Sutton Trust Summer School, and Glasgow does not publish the A-level grades.
contextual.rulesText: Glasgow says it operates contextualised admissions for applicants living in Scotland. The groups it lists for guaranteed adjusted offers are people living in a Scottish postcode area in SIMD deciles 1-4 (MD20/40), people with care experience, estranged from family, carers, people seeking asylum and people with refugee status. Adjusted grades are published for Scottish Highers only, not A-levels. Completing a Glasgow pre-entry programme (including the Sutton Trust Summer School) 'may lead to' an adjusted offer.

source.evidence: we operate a system of contextualised admissions for applicants living in Scotland.

notes: Scottish university: these degrees are 4 years (Honours in years 3 and 4) and years 1 and 2 also include other subjects. Glasgow's degree pages are for entry in 2027; no 2028 pages yet (checked 2026-10-21), so all courses use 2027 entry.

Glasgow's degree pages fill in the A-level entry requirements with a degree picker and a country picker. This record uses the England selection for every course (Wales and Northern Ireland show the same A-level requirements for Economics).

Standard A-level offer is AAB for every course recorded. Glasgow's published widening-access (adjusted) offers are for Scottish Highers and applicants living in Scotland, so no lower A-level offer is recorded.

The only route to an adjusted offer for Year 12 students from England, Wales or Northern Ireland is the Sutton Trust Summer School hosted at Glasgow (recorded in each course's alternative offers). Glasgow's own Top-Up, Reach, Access to a Career, Taster Week and WP Summer School programmes are for pupils in Scotland, SIMD postcode areas or school leavers holding an adjusted offer, so none is listed as a programme.
No admissions test: Glasgow is not on UAT-UK's TMUA list for 2027 entry and none is listed in the entry requirements shown for these courses.

Glasgow RUK Access Bursary (2027-28 entry): £2,500 a year if household income is under £25,001, £1,500 a year if between £25,000 and £35,000. RUK Excellence Scholarship: £3,000 for the first year for A*AA or better at A-level in one sitting (fees page).

Other economics joint degrees on Glasgow's Economics page (not recorded as separate courses, England selection): Economics/Business & Management LN12 (AAB, English or Humanities, Mathematics), Economics/Accountancy BAcc LN14 (AAB, Mathematics at A, English or Humanities, GCSE English B or 5/6), Mathematics/Economics BSc LG1D and Economics/Statistics BSc GL31 (AAB, Mathematics at A), Economics/Philosophy LVC5 (as Economics).

Postcode is the Adam Smith Building, 2 Discovery Place, home of the Adam Smith Business School that runs these degrees; Glasgow says its main entrance faces the main University campus and Kelvingrove Park. The degree pages say the courses are taught at the Gilmorehill campus.

contextual.summary: Goldsmiths gives a contextual offer three grades lower than its published offer to care-experienced and estranged applicants, and gives other flagged applications extra consideration (no guaranteed offer).
contextual.typicalReduction: Three grades lower than the published requirement for care-experienced or estranged applicants (a typical A-level offer of CCC would be reduced to DDD); students on a Progression Agreement can get offers one grade lower than advertised.

criteria.detail: Care experienced: time in residential care, foster care or kinship care (formal or informal) or as an unaccompanied asylum seeker. Answer yes to the care-experienced question on your UCAS application. Goldsmiths sets no limit on how long you were in care and no age limit.

Estranged: no contact with your parents during your studies, or very limited contact where you still have a relationship with your siblings. Answer yes to the estranged question on your UCAS application. Goldsmiths sets no limit on how long you were estranged and no age limit.

Progression Agreements (local and mature students): students on agreements with Goldsmiths' local partner colleges (the page names Lewisham College, Southwark College and Mulberry UTC) or studying an OCN or LASER Access to HE Diploma can access guaranteed interviews and/or offers one grade lower than advertised on more than 50 undergraduate programmes. contextual.rulesText: If you answer yes to either the care experienced or estranged questions on your UCAS application, Goldsmiths will automatically consider you for a reduced grade offer (three grades lower than the published requirement; the exact offer depends on the programme and qualification). contextual.summary: UK (Home fee) applicants who meet at least one of Herts' criteria are considered automatically for a contextual offer, typically up to one grade lower (about eight UCAS points).
contextual.typicalReduction: Typically up to one grade lower than the standard entry requirements (equivalent to eight UCAS points)

criteria.detail: You received free school meals at any point in the last six years during secondary education.
You were in care before the age of 16.
You care, unpaid, for a friend or family member with an illness or disability, mental health condition or an addiction.
You are irreconcilably estranged from both parents and receive no support from them.
You are a Home fee applicant with refugee status.
Your home postcode (from your UCAS form) falls into IMD Quintile 1, the areas facing the most significant socioeconomic challenges (IMD decile 1-2).
Gypsy, Roma, Traveller, Showmen and Boater applicants: email the Student Success team with your full name and UCAS number to be considered for a contextual offer.

contextual.rulesText: To be considered, you must be a UK domiciled student with Home fee status and meet at least one of the criteria. If you meet them, the admissions team considers you for a contextual offer automatically. Grade adjustments are not available for part-time applicants, deferred entry or Clearing, and for some courses adjustments may not be possible.

source.evidence: A contextual offer is typically up to one grade lower than our standard entry requirements (equivalent to eight UCAS points).

contextual.summary: If you meet two or more of Hull's criteria you can get a contextual offer of 96 UCAS points, applied automatically from your UCAS application.
contextual.typicalReduction: A contextual offer is 96 UCAS points, which Hull says is lower than its standard entry requirements (on the economics and business courses recorded here the typical offer is 96 to 112 points, so it equals the bottom of that range).

criteria.detail: You live in an area with a low number of young people progressing to higher education (Hull's summary page: an area with historically low progression to higher education or an area of high relative deprivation). Hull doesn't name the measure or quintiles.
You are a carer.
You have parenting responsibilities.
You are care experienced (have spent time in local authority care).
You are from a military family.
You are a refugee or asylum seeker.
You are, or have been, eligible for free school meals.
You are the first person in your family to attend higher education (neither parent or guardian attended university).
You are aged over 21.
You have a disability.
You are a member of the Gypsy, Traveller, Roma, Showmen or Boater communities.
You are estranged from your family.
You have other relevant circumstances that aren't listed.

contextual.rulesText: You may qualify for a contextual offer if you meet two or more of the listed criteria. If you qualify, Hull applies the offer automatically from your UCAS application (admissions staff assess your circumstances and assign qualifying points). Offers can be made to home and international applicants completing UK qualifications that carry UCAS tariff points. Not available for Foundation Year entry or programmes with mandatory placements or capped student numbers; the listed exclusions are BA British Politics & Legislative Studies, LLB Law & Legislative Studies, BA Primary Teaching with Foundation Year and health programmes such as nursing and midwifery.

source.evidence: You may be eligible for a contextual offer if you meet two or more of our criteria.

notes: Hull's offers are in UCAS tariff points: 96 to 112 points on every course recorded (112 points is shown as A levels BBC). At least 80 points must come from A levels, BTEC or equivalent qualifications.
A contextual offer is 96 UCAS points, the bottom of the typical range on these courses; you need to meet two or more of Hull's contextual criteria.

contextual.summary: Applicants from England or Wales who meet any one of Kent's contextual criteria get a conditional offer up to 16 UCAS points (about two A level grades) lower than the standard offer.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to 16 UCAS points lower than the University standard offer; for A levels, up to two grades below the published standard offer. Course-specific subject grades are not adjusted. On Kent's course pages the contextual offers are shown, e.g. CCD/CCC for Economics and BCC for Accounting and Finance.

criteria.detail: Live in a Tundra Q1 area
Live in an IMD 2019 Q1 or Q2 area
A mature student, aged 21 or over on the 1st day of term
Free School Meals recipient
Have spent any time in Care under a Local Authority
Disabled students and those with long term health conditions, including learning differences and mental health conditions
Young carers
Unaccompanied Minors, asylum seekers and refugees
Applicants from Gypsy, Traveler, Roma and Showman Boater Communities
Applicants from Military Families
Attend an English school/college that receives below average KS5 academic qualification results (identified using the Applicant Centre or Exam Institution on the UCAS application)
Documented mitigating circumstances
Applicants with significant, documented, education gaps

contextual.rulesText: Contextual offers are for applicants domiciled in England or Wales who meet one or more of the criteria. Say on your UCAS application how you meet them (or in your personal statement or reference); Kent may ask for evidence. Kent uses datasets available as of 1 October each year.

source.evidence: Contextual offers are up to 16 UCAS points lower than the University Standard Offer

criteria.detail: Received Free School Meals during secondary education, as declared on your UCAS application

notes: All course facts are for September 2027 entry: Lancaster's course pages offer 2027 and 2026 in their entry-year picker, and the 2028 address redirects to 2027.
Lancaster isn't on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry, and none of the recorded course pages mentions an admissions test or interview.

BSc Economics (L100) and Economics and Finance (NL31) need A-level Maths. BA Economics, Business Economics, Economics and Politics, PPE and Geography and Economics don't, but they need GCSE Maths grade 6/B (Lancaster's qualifications page says that where it asks for GCSE Maths 6/B it often considers a slightly lower grade case by case, for example if you take A-level Maths, but these course pages don't say so).
Geography and Economics (LL71) suits Geography and Psychology A-levels: Lancaster recommends Geography and also lists Psychology among the accepted subjects.
Most courses have separate UCAS codes for the 4-year placement ('Industry') and study abroad versions; Home fees for those years are 20% and 15% of the standard fee.

Also offered but not recorded, to keep to 8 courses: Mathematics, Operational Research, Statistics and Economics (MORSE, GLN0), Finance (N300), Accounting and Finance (N400) and Business Management (N102).

contextual.summary: Leeds' Access to Leeds scheme gives UK applicants who meet at least two of its criteria an offer up to two grades lower than the standard offer (for example ABB instead of AAA) if they also pass its module, and applicants from Low Participation Neighbourhoods may get one grade off automatically.
contextual.typicalReduction: Access to Leeds: up to two grades lower than the standard offer (for example AAA becomes ABB). Low Participation Neighbourhoods: usually one A-level grade lower.

criteria.detail: Your parents or carers did not go to university: they have not completed an undergraduate degree at a university or polytechnic in the UK or overseas. You also count if they started but did not finish a degree, hold an HNC or HND, an Open University or similar distance-learning degree, a part-time work-based degree, or a degree but you are estranged from them with little or no contact.

Your permanent home postcode (as on your UCAS application) is in an area with low levels of participation in higher education and/or high levels of socioeconomic deprivation, measured against government data. Leeds does not name the dataset on this page.

Household income of £25,000 or below, or you were eligible for free school meals at any point during secondary school (also shown by receiving the 16-19 Bursary Fund or Learner Support because your income is £25,000 or below, or by a parent or carer income declaration). Together these count as one criterion.

You attended or attend a school that performed below the national average at GCSE (its Attainment 8 score compared with the England average). Independent fee-paying schools are not eligible under this criterion.

Your personal circumstances have had a disruptive impact on your education, for example caring responsibilities or being a young carer, a recent close family bereavement, estrangement from your parents or carers, a mental or physical health condition or disability, being from a military service family, or refugee or asylum seeker status. Several instances count as one criterion.

You are a care leaver or have experienced time in care: any time in local authority or formal kinship care, adopted from care, or on a child protection plan after age 11. Care leavers (at least 13 weeks in local authority care spanning their 16th birthday) also count under the personal circumstances criterion.

contextual.rulesText: Access to Leeds: you must meet at least two separate criteria from the personal circumstances list, and also meet all the applicant requirements (UK applicant applying through UCAS to a full-time undergraduate course, holding or studying the required level 3 qualifications, no existing undergraduate degree, not taking a foundation course, no Access to HE Diploma except for Healthcare degrees). Leeds must be your firm choice and you need to pass the Access to Leeds module. Separately, if you live in a Low Participation Neighbourhood (assessed with the Indices of Multiple Deprivation), your offer could be reduced by one A-level grade in most cases; you do not apply separately.

contextual.summary: Lincoln automatically considers Home (UK) fee applicants who meet its criteria for a contextual offer one grade lower than the standard offer (for example 104 instead of 112 UCAS Tariff points, BCC instead of BBC).
contextual.typicalReduction: One grade (8 UCAS Tariff points) lower than the standard entry requirements for most undergraduate courses, from a minimum of two full A levels or equivalent (e.g. 112 points / BBC becomes 104 points / BCC).

criteria.detail: You live in an area with a high level of deprivation or a low number of people going to university (usually decided by your postcode), or you live in a Lincolnshire local authority area.

Your school or college's academic performance is lower than the national average, or a small number of its pupils go on to higher education. Schools in Lincoln's Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) partnership get the same reduction in tariff.
You receive, or have received, free school meals (the UCAS application asks you to confirm this).
You are a care leaver (tick the 'in care' box on the UCAS application form).
You have a disability, including long-term health conditions.

contextual.rulesText: If you meet Lincoln's general criteria for a contextual offer you are asked to achieve one grade lower than the standard entry requirements for most undergraduate courses, from a minimum of two full A levels or equivalent. You don't need to do anything extra: apply through UCAS and you are automatically considered. You must be a Home (UK) fee payer; contextual offers only apply to full-time undergraduate courses (foundation programmes are excluded). Any subject-specific requirements must still be met. The criteria listed are Lincoln's '2026 Entry' wording.

source.evidence: If you meet our general criteria for a contextual offer, we will ask you to achieve one grade lower than the standard entry requirements for the majority of our undergraduate degree courses.

notes: Lincoln publishes entry requirements as UCAS Tariff points from at least two A levels (Economics and Accountancy and Finance 104 to 112 points; Business and Management 96 to 104 points), with BBC (or BCC for Business and Management) given as the A level equivalent of the top of the range. Its offer guide says other grade mixes such as ABC can reach 112 points, and an EPQ can be counted once two A levels are achieved.
No admissions test: Lincoln is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry and no course page names a test.

Care experienced: you have spent any amount of time in Local Authority care before your 18th birthday and meet the nationally used eligibility criteria (UK students).

contextual.rulesText: Reduced offers are automatic (no extra form): you get an offer of up to two grades below the standard offer if your postcode is in IMD Quintile 1 or you have spent any time in social care. Where a range is used, the standard offer is the upper grade profile. If you qualify for a reduction for more than one reason, it stays at a maximum of two grades. Other contextual indicators (for example disability, disrupted studies, UCAS MEM data) are used for additional consideration, such as at interview or on results day, not for an automatic reduced offer.

source.evidence: up to a 2-grade reduction* from the standard offer ... Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD) Deciles 1 and 2 ... UK Care Experienced students

fees.text: £10,050 a year for UK (Home) students on full-time courses starting in September 2027 (2027/28), subject to Parliamentary approval. A different, reduced fee is charged in sandwich (placement) years and years abroad. From 2028/29 the fee cap may rise each year with inflation.

source.evidence: The Government has confirmed that this cap will be £9,790 for 2026/27 and £10,050 for 2027/28, in both cases subject to Parliamentary approval.

contextual.summary: If you answer 'yes' to any one of LJMU's UCAS widening participation questions (estranged, unpaid carer, parent, armed forces connection, free school meals, care experienced), or took part in targeted LJMU Outreach activity, you get an offer lower than the typical entry requirements.

criteria.detail: Estranged from both parents (not in contact with and supported by either of them): answers 'yes' to this UCAS widening participation question.
Has unpaid caring responsibilities (not including parenting): answers 'yes' to this UCAS question.
Is a parent or has parenting responsibilities for a child aged 17 or under: answers 'yes' to this UCAS question.
Has a parent or carer who currently serves in the UK Armed Forces, or has done so in the past: answers 'yes' to this UCAS question.
Has ever served in the UK Armed Forces: answers 'yes' to this UCAS question.
Currently receiving free school meals, or received them at any point between the ages of 11 and 18: answers 'yes' to this UCAS question.
Has been in care, or is care experienced: answers 'yes' to this UCAS question.
Took part in targeted LJMU Outreach activity (programmes are not named on the page).

criteria.detail: Known to be eligible for free school meals at the end of Key Stage 4 (Year 11) and/or the six years before it (England; equivalent rules for Northern Ireland and Wales), or currently receiving free school meals or free meals in further education
Live in an area in IMD quintile 1 (England only) AND attend a non-fee-paying (state) school or college
Taking part in Realising Opportunities: you get a dual offer including an alternative offer up to two grades lower, dependent on completing the programme
Taking part in LUDUS Gold: you get a dual offer including an alternative offer up to three grades lower, dependent on completing the programme
Spent more than three months in care (considered as contextual information; not listed as an Access Loughborough criterion)
Have caring responsibilities (young carer); supporting evidence from your referee is needed
Estranged from your family
Recognised refugee, asylum seeker or granted humanitarian protection
Disability or long-term health condition (supporting evidence from your referee needed)
Mature applicant: aged 21 or over at the start of the course
Other personal or extenuating circumstances that disrupted your education

contextual.rulesText: You're eligible for an Access Loughborough Contextual Offer if you were known to be eligible for free school meals (or currently receive them), or you attend a state school or college and live in IMD quintile 1 (England only). It is open to applicants taking three A levels, or two A levels plus an accepted Level 3 qualification, who expect to pay UK fees. If you're eligible, any offer will be up to two grades lower than typical, but eligibility doesn't guarantee an offer. Other contextual information (care, caring responsibilities, disability, estrangement, refugee status, mature age, extenuating circumstances) is considered individually and may lead to a reduced offer of up to one grade lower.

source.evidence: Where specific contextual information is met, you will be eligible for an Access Loughborough Contextual Offer. This is up to two grades lower than typical entry requirements.

notes: All course facts are for September 2027 entry; Loughborough hasn't published 2028-entry pages yet.

Economics, Economics and Finance and Economics and Management say A-level Maths is not essential, but they need GCSE Maths grade 6 (grade 5 for Finance and Accounting and Finance). Mathematics with Economics needs A-level Maths at grade A.
Every course has a 4-year version with an optional placement year (separate UCAS code) and a year abroad option; the placement year fee is 20% of the full-time fee and a study-abroad year 15%.
Loughborough doesn't normally include the EPQ in offer conditions; it may be used when considering an application after exam results.
Realising Opportunities gives a dual offer up to two grades lower than typical; LUDUS Gold gives one up to three A-level grades lower. Both are recorded as alternative offers on each course.
Many courses get a large number of applications per place, and meeting the typical offer doesn't guarantee an offer.
Business and Management BSc (N202, typical offer AAB) was not added, to keep to 8 courses.

contextual.summary: If you have Home fee status and meet any one of LSE's contextual flags (care-experienced, free school meals in the last six years, a lowest-participation home area, or an LSE or Sutton Trust access programme), you may be considered for a contextual offer one or two grades lower.
contextual.typicalReduction: One or two grades lower than the standard entry requirements, depending on the degree programme. Any Maths requirement must still be met.

criteria.detail: You are a care-experienced student: you have spent time living with foster carers under local authority care, in residential care (for example a children's home), looked after at home under a supervision order, or in kinship care with relatives or friends (officially or informally).
You have been eligible for free school meals (FSM) within the previous six years. Tick the FSM question on UCAS and ask your teacher to confirm it in their reference.
Your home postcode is in TUNDRA Quintile 1 (the 20% lowest for university participation) if you live in England. If you live in another UK nation LSE uses the POLAR4 dataset instead.

You have completed an intensive LSE widening participation programme (LSE Springboard, LSE Thrive, LSE Pathways to Law or LSE Pathways to Banking and Finance) or any Sutton Trust Pathways programme at a UK university (Engineering, Medicine, Law, Banking and Finance or Consulting).

contextual.rulesText: You may be eligible for a contextual offer if you have Home fee status and meet one or more of the criteria. LSE flags the information automatically from your UCAS form. Contextual offer grades are listed on each programme page. Having a contextual flag does not guarantee an offer, and LSE also uses other contextual information for extra consideration rather than a lower offer.

source.evidence: You may be eligible for a contextual offer if you have Home fee status and meet one or more of the criteria below.

notes: No 2028-entry course pages yet (checked 2026-10-21): the newest LSE course pages are for 2027 entry (academic year 2027/28, start 27 September 2027), so courses use 2027 entry. BSc Geography with Economics only shows 2026-entry requirements (2027 entry 'still subject to confirmation').

TMUA (2027 entry): mandatory for BSc Economics and BSc Econometrics and Mathematical Economics; recommended but not mandatory for Mathematics and Economics and Economics and Data Science (and other maths programmes). Not used for Politics and Economics, PPE, Geography with Economics or Finance.

LSE says it received approximately 34,000 applications for roughly 1,900 places in 2026 (whole university, not per course). Per-course application, intake and ratio figures (labelled 2025) are on most programme pages and are recorded under each course's competition.
LSE does not interview candidates. Its UCAS deadline for September 2027 entry is 13 January 2027 at 18:00.

Contextual offers are one or two grades lower than the standard offer, and any Maths requirement must still be met. Completing LSE Pathways to Law or any Sutton Trust Pathways programme (Engineering, Medicine, Law, Banking and Finance, Consulting) also counts as a contextual flag; LSE Pathways to Law is not listed under programmes because it is a law programme.
LSE halls: rates start from £100 a week for a shared self-catered room (accommodation prices page). Private housing in London starts at about £650 a month (London on a budget page).

Other LSE degrees with Economics exist but are not recorded here: Accounting and Finance, Economics and Economic History, Mathematics with Economics, Philosophy and Economics, Management and Economic History.

criteria.detail: Home postcode in ACORN category 5 (Stretched Society) or 6 (Low Income Living). The postcode alone gives a WP flag, not a contextual offer.
Home postcode in TUNDRA quintile 1 (higher education participation). The postcode alone gives a WP flag, not a contextual offer.
Home postcode in IMD quintile 1 (disadvantage). The postcode alone gives a WP flag, not a contextual offer.
GCSE or A-level school/college performed below the national average (averaged over up to three years); together with the postcode criteria this gives a WP Plus flag.
Eligible for free school meals during secondary education (England, Northern Ireland, Wales; checked from official data, not self-declared); gives a WP Plus flag.
In care in the UK for more than three months; gives a WP Plus PLUS flag.
Permission to stay in the UK as a refugee, asylum seeker, under humanitarian protection or on a Ukraine scheme; gives a WP Plus PLUS flag.
Young adult carer (under 25 on 1 September of the year of entry, UK resident); gives a WP Plus PLUS flag.

Completed the Manchester Access Programme (Year 12, Greater Manchester): reduced offer of up to two grades. The Arthur Lewis Assignment gives Social Sciences offer-holders a one-grade reduction and the Manchester Distance Access Scheme gives eligible offer-holders on some other courses a one-grade reduction.

contextual.rulesText: WP flag = home postcode meets the ACORN, TUNDRA or IMD criteria. WP Plus flag = postcode criteria plus a below-average school, or free school meals. WP Plus PLUS flag = refugee/asylum/humanitarian protection/Ukraine scheme, care for more than three months, or young adult carer. Contextual offers only apply to WP Plus or WP Plus PLUS applicants whose course has standard entry requirements of ABB or higher and who meet the published entry requirements. Applicants are assessed automatically from their UCAS form; the postcode and school checks are for UK applicants under 21 only.

source.evidence: If you meet our WP Plus criteria, the contextual offer is usually one grade lower than the standard entry requirements.

contextual.summary: Applicants who meet one or more contextual criteria may get an offer up to two grades below the typical entry requirements, with no separate application.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to two grades below the typical entry requirements

criteria.detail: Your home postcode is in POLAR4 Quintile 1 or 2: a neighbourhood with a low rate of progression to higher education. Newcastle has a postcode checker.
You have experienced any time in care during your life.

You are estranged from your family and no longer have support due to a breakdown in that relationship (this may include biological, adoptive or step-parents, or other family members who previously provided support).
You are eligible for free school meals. If you attend an independent school but would have been eligible in the state sector, you may also qualify (checked with data supplied by UCAS).
You have sole or shared responsibility for the care of a relative because they are ill, have a disability, are experiencing mental distress, or are affected by substance abuse.
You attend a state school in North East England (Regional Contextual Offer).

contextual.rulesText: You may be eligible if you meet one or more of the criteria. There is no separate application: make sure the relevant information is in the 'Applicant Context' section of your UCAS application. Eligibility for a contextual offer does not guarantee that an offer will be made.

source.evidence: Eligible applicants may receive an offer of up to two grades below the typical entry requirements.

notes: All six courses use 2027 entry: each course page says its requirements and offers apply to 2027 entry (start September 2027). No 2028-entry pages are published yet.

No course page names an admissions test and Newcastle is not on UAT-UK's TMUA list for 2027 entry. Mathematics and Economics (GL11) accepts grade 2 in any STEP paper as an alternative to a second listed A level.

Economics, Economics and Finance, Economics and Business Management and Finance share the same headline offer (AAB excluding General Studies); Politics and Economics is AAB with General Studies accepted; Mathematics and Economics needs an A in Mathematics.

Alternative offers (access-schemes page): contextual, Regional Contextual, High Performance Athlete and Realising Opportunities are each up to 2 grades lower; PARTNERS is up to 3 grades lower. Pathways to Newcastle (up to 2 grades lower) covers science, maths and engineering courses only.

Regional offers apply only to people who live or study in the North East or Tees Valley: a Regional Guaranteed Offer for eligible postcodes and a Regional Contextual Offer (up to two grades lower) for state-school students in the region; both need predicted CCC or above and the course's subject requirements.

Opportunity Scholarships (cash bursaries, awarded automatically by household income): £2,000 a year (up to £25,000), £1,250 (£25,001-£35,000), £750 (£35,001-£40,000). The page does not say which year these amounts apply to.

Campus postcode NE1 4SE is the Business School (5 Barrack Road), where the economics and finance courses are taught; the University's main postal address is NE1 7RU. Newcastle also runs Experience Days (Years 12 and 13) for school groups, not researched.

contextual.summary: Home-fee applicants who meet any one of Northumbria's contextual criteria and firmly accept their offer need fewer UCAS tariff points on results day (for example 96 instead of 112).
contextual.typicalReduction: 120-point course to 104 points; 112-point course to 96 points; 72-point course to 56 points

criteria.detail: Your home address on your UCAS application is in POLAR4 quintile 1 or 2 (an area with a low rate of progression to higher education).
Your home address on your UCAS application is in IMD decile 1-4 (areas of higher deprivation; deciles 1-4 are the bottom two quintiles).
You have spent time in care. You must complete the care questions in your UCAS form; Northumbria may ask for evidence.
Black, Asian or Minority Ethnic origin (an under-represented group at Northumbria). UCAS passes this on late, so you complete Northumbria's Contextual Offer Enquiry short form.
You are eligible for free school meals.
Adult learner: over 21 at the start of your programme.
You listed unpaid caring responsibilities (not including parenting) on your UCAS form; Northumbria may ask for evidence.
Estranged from parents: not in contact with or supported by parents.
Physical and/or mental health condition, long term illness or learning difference.
Student parent: you are a parent or have parental responsibilities for a child under 17.
You have served or are serving in the UK Armed Forces, or a parent or guardian has served or is serving.
First generation: you do not have a parent who holds a higher education qualification.
Refugee or humanitarian status, or currently claiming asylum (extra evidence is required).
Member of the Gypsy, Traveller, Roma, Showman or Boater communities.
You took part in the HAF+ programme or the Holiday Hope (London) programme.

contextual.rulesText: You are eligible if you meet any one of the criteria and firmly accept your offer via UCAS. You must be eligible for home fees, apply through UCAS (with the information entered on your application) and hold Level 3 qualifications that attract UCAS tariff points. Your UCAS offer isn't changed: the lower points are applied when results arrive. The reduction can't be combined with a reduced offer from Northumbria's other Supported Entry Scheme or Extenuating Circumstances. If you miss the lower points on results day, Northumbria guarantees a place on an extended degree (foundation year) course if you firmly accepted.

source.evidence: You are eligible for contextual admissions if you meet any of the criteria below and firmly accept your offer via UCAS.

notes: No 2028-entry offers yet (checked 2026-10-21): every course page shows 'Entry Requirements 2027/28' and a September 2027 start, so all courses use 2027 entry.
Northumbria gives offers in UCAS tariff points, not grades: the standard offer is 112 points on all six courses recorded and the contextual offer is 96 points.
Northumbria is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry, and no course page names an admissions test.

Extended Degrees (4 years including a foundation year) exist for these subjects. The Economics Extended Degree (UCAS Z018) has a standard offer of 72 UCAS points and a contextual offer of 56 (https://www.northumbria.ac.uk/study-at-northumbria/courses/bsc-hons-economics-extended-degree-uusxic1/). The 2027/28 fee for a classroom-based foundation year is £5,760.

Aspirational offers: Northumbria typically makes standard tariff offers to applicants whose predicted grades are equivalent to up to three or four grades below its standard entry criteria, depending on the programme, and in most cases adds a reserve 'dual offer' for the Extended Degree (https://www.northumbria.ac.uk/study-at-northumbria/admissions/northumbria-university-entry-requirements-essential-information/aspirational-offers/).
Halls prices come from each residence page, which says 'Prices for 2026/27': the lowest is the Stephenson Bronze bedroom (£121.05 a week) and the highest the Camden Court studio (£238.92 a week).
Evolve (post-16 workshops for Year 12-13) is booked by schools and colleges rather than applied for by individual students, so it is not listed as a programme.

contextual.summary: Nottingham makes a standard contextual offer (usually one grade lower) or an enhanced contextual offer (usually two grades lower) to Home students at UK non-fee-paying schools who meet one criterion; it's applied automatically from your UCAS form.
contextual.typicalReduction: Standard contextual: usually one grade lower; enhanced contextual: usually two grades lower (subject grades generally stay). Business School courses: standard contextual offer ABB.

criteria.detail: Live in an area with high levels of deprivation (University postcode checker) - standard offer
Refugee status from the Home Office - standard offer
Spent more than three months in care - standard offer
Completed a Sutton Trust post-16 programme not hosted by Nottingham (including Sutton Trust Online) - standard offer
Received free school meals on any census day in the 6 years up to the end of key stage 4 (verified via UCAS) - enhanced offer

Completed a Nottingham outreach programme: Sutton Trust Summer School at Nottingham, Sutton Trust Pathways to Medicine or Veterinary Medicine at Nottingham, Ambition 16-18 (Tier 1 / Tier 1+), or Realising Opportunities (Cohort 15 - 2024/25 and Cohort 16 - 2025/26 completers only) - enhanced offer

contextual.rulesText: You must have Home-UK fee status and your current or most recent school/college must be in the UK and not independent (fee-paying), except refugees and care leavers. 'One of the following must also apply' for a standard offer; for an enhanced offer 'You must also meet one of the following'. Young carers and disability are not contextual criteria.

source.evidence: To qualify for a standard contextual offer, you must have Home-UK fee status and your current or most recent school/college must be in the UK and cannot be an independent (fee-paying) school/college. ... One of the following must also apply:

notes: Nottingham gives contextual offers for national programmes: a completed Sutton Trust post-16 programme not hosted by Nottingham (incl. Sutton Trust Online) qualifies for a standard contextual offer; the Sutton Trust Summer School at Nottingham and Realising Opportunities (only 2024/25 and 2025/26 completers listed) qualify for an enhanced contextual offer.
School of Economics courses don't require A-level Maths for Economics or PPE, but taking Maths lowers the offer from A*AA to AAA.

Additional Qualifications Offer Reduction Scheme: grade A in an EPQ (or eligible Core Maths / extra AS level) gives a one grade reduced offer; it never goes below the University minimum of BBC and doesn't combine with an enhanced contextual offer.
Business School courses (Industrial Economics, Finance Accounting and Management, Business and Management) are taught at Jubilee Campus in Nottingham, not University Park.
Also offered but not recorded: Economics and International Economics BSc (L160), A*AA or AAA with A-level Maths.
Young carers and disabled applicants aren't covered by contextual offers; Nottingham asks them to use its extenuating circumstances form instead.

criteria.detail: Currently studying at Nottingham College, Vision West Notts College, Bilborough College, Confetti, on an NTU college course, or at one of NTU's named key feeder schools or colleges (full list on the page), and progressing to a full-time foundation, integrated foundation or undergraduate degree at NTU.
East Midlands postcode: home postcode is within the East Midlands devolved authority covering Derbyshire, Nottinghamshire, Derby and Nottingham.
Low participation areas: from an area of low participation in higher education, according to the Office for Students' Participation of Local Areas data (POLAR 4, quintile 1 or 2).
Care experienced: spent time in local authority care, foster care, or any formal care setting.
Free School Meals: may have received Free School Meals during secondary education.
Estranged from parents: you have no contact or support from your family.
Elite athletes: applicants who show exceptional sporting potential.

contextual.rulesText: You are guaranteed a contextual offer if you meet any of the listed criteria.
