contextual.summary: UK applicants who meet one of Brookes' contextual criteria (for example lived in care, refugee status, free school meals, young carer under 25, or completed Brookes Engage), or a school-results plus area combination, can get a contextual offer shown on each course page.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to 3 grades below the standard entry requirements

criteria.detail: You have lived in local authority care.
Your residential status is 'refugee' or 'humanitarian protection'.
You have participated in the Brookes Engage sustained outreach programmes.
You are eligible for free school meals.
You are under 25 and have caring responsibilities.
You attend a school where average performance is below average at GCSE or in the bottom 40% nationally at A level (or equivalent). Listed as part of a combination with an area criterion.

You live in an area of low participation in higher education, or in an area of higher socio-economic disadvantage. Listed as part of a combination with the school criterion; the page does not name the measure used.

contextual.rulesText: UK students applying for an undergraduate degree (excluding foundation years and foundation degrees) may be eligible for a contextual offer if ONE of these applies: lived in local authority care; refugee or humanitarian protection status; took part in the Brookes Engage sustained outreach programmes; eligible for free school meals; under 25 with caring responsibilities. You may also be eligible if you meet a combination of: attending a school where average performance is below average at GCSE or in the bottom 40% nationally at A level (or equivalent), AND living in an area of low participation in higher education OR living in an area of higher socio-economic disadvantage (the page does not say exactly how these three are grouped). There is no separate form: apply through UCAS and indicate your residential status or care history if relevant.

source.evidence: Our contextual offer is a grade reduction of up to 3 grades below the standard entry requirements.

notes: Offers are set in UCAS Tariff points, with an A-level grade example (e.g. 128 points = ABB). Brookes says it makes conditional offers using the UCAS Tariff wherever possible, so AS levels, the Extended Project and other tariff qualifications can count towards the points.

contextual.summary: If one or more of Plymouth's criteria apply to you (for example free school meals, time in care, an IMD Quintile 1 postcode or a listed South West/Wales school), a lower contextual offer may be applied automatically.
contextual.typicalReduction: Typically 8 UCAS points below the advertised tariff on the business school courses; Plymouth says up to three grades below the standard offer

criteria.detail: You have spent three months or more in local authority care (tick the care question on your UCAS application).
You attend a state secondary school and are or have been eligible for free school meals.
You have refugee status or humanitarian protection.
You are from a military family: either or both of your parents have served in the UK Armed Forces.
You have ever served in the UK Armed Forces.
You are a member of the Gypsy, Traveller, Roma, Showmen or Boater communities.
You are aged 18 to 24 and not communicating with, or supported by, either parent or carer because of an irreconcilable breakdown (this includes parents or carers who have died or can't be traced).
You attend a non-selective state school or college in the South West/Wales region on Plymouth's list of schools.
You come from an area in Indices of Multiple Deprivation (IMD) Quintile 1; the page has a postcode checker.

contextual.rulesText: If one or more of the criteria applies to you, a contextual offer may automatically be applied by the Admissions team (you do not need to do anything else). Plymouth uses the widening access questions on the UCAS form. Meeting a criterion does not guarantee an offer. The page says contextual offers are not available for foundation year degrees or programmes with mandatory placements or capped numbers (including medicine and dentistry).

contextual.summary: Queen Mary makes standard contextual offers (up to two grades lower) and enhanced contextual offers (up to three grades lower) to Home applicants who meet one of its criteria.
contextual.typicalReduction: Standard contextual offer: up to two grades below the standard A-level offer; enhanced contextual offer: up to three grades below

criteria.detail: Live in an area of disadvantage defined using ACORN (groups M, N, P, Q, R, S or U)
Received free school meals on any day before finishing Key Stage 4 (Year 11)
Your school or college is sponsored by Queen Mary (Drapers' Academy, St Paul's Way Trust School or Royal Greenwich Trust School)
Your GCSE and/or A-level school or college performed below the national average over the last three years — counts only if you also live in an IMD quintile 1 or 2 area
Home postcode in IMD quintile 1 or 2 — counts only together with a below-average-performing school
Care experienced (standard offer); care leavers get the enhanced offer
Estranged (aged 18–24 and not communicating with either parent)
You have a declared disability
Immigration permission confirming you are a refugee, an asylum seeker, or entered via a Ukraine scheme
Successfully completed Access to Queen Mary or Realising Opportunities (enhanced offer); Bridge the Gap and Pathways to Law count for Medicine/Dentistry and Law only

contextual.rulesText: To be eligible you must meet one of the listed criteria (the school-performance criterion only counts together with an IMD area). Enhanced offers are for care leavers and those who complete a Queen Mary sustained/partnered access scheme. Home fee status only; A-levels, Scottish Highers and IB are eligible.

source.evidence: Our standard contextual offer is up to a two grade reduction from our standard A-level offer

Queen Mary Business School is getting a new building near Mile End station in 2027 (stated on the Business Management and Accounting and Finance pages).

contextual.summary: Applicants who meet at least one of Reading's contextual criteria (for example a low-participation or deprived postcode, a declared disability, care experience, or taking part in Reading Scholars) get an offer typically two grades lower.
contextual.typicalReduction: Typically two grades lower than the top end of the published grade range (for example ABB becomes BBC); one grade lower again if you are taking an EPQ.

criteria.detail: Live in an area with low participation in higher education (POLAR quintiles 1 and 2). You must be classed as a 'Home' student and have the correct Postal/Home postcode on your UCAS form. The page does not say which POLAR version.
Live in an area with high levels of deprivation (IMD quintiles 1 and 2). You must be classed as a 'Home' student and have the correct Postal/Home postcode on your UCAS form.
Have declared a disability on your UCAS form (choose the most appropriate option from the disability list).
Took part in Reading's Reading Scholars programme (contact outreach@reading.ac.uk for details).
Care experienced (select this category on your UCAS form).
Refugees or asylum seekers (select this category on your UCAS form).
Estranged from your family (select this category on your UCAS form).
Young carer: responsible for unpaid care for a family member, partner or friend who could not cope without your support; you must be 25 or under.

Child of a military family (service child): a parent or guardian currently serving in the UK Regular Armed Forces or as a reservist, or who has done so at any point in the first 25 years of your life; you must be 25 or under.

contextual.rulesText: Contextual offers go to applicants who meet at least one of the listed criteria. The offer applies whether Reading is your firm or insurance choice, and you still need any subject-specific and GCSE requirements. If you are also taking an EPQ the contextual offer is lowered by one more grade (for example BBB becomes BBC). No contextual offers are made for programmes with a Foundation Year.

fees.text: £10,050 per year for UK (Home) students starting in 2027/28. Different fees apply to some Foundation Year and accelerated degree courses and to a year spent abroad or working in industry. Fees are reviewed each year and may rise for continuing students.

source.evidence: The tuition fee for students starting their degree in 2027/28 will be £10,050 for that year.

livingCosts.text: Undergraduate halls at Egham cost about £111–£258 a week in 2026/27 (£111.02 is a shared bedroom in Founder's Building; en-suite rooms are mostly £204–£258). Halls such as George Eliot, Gowar and Founder's are on 38-week contracts (September to June). Bills and internet are included; Founder's and Reid are catered (one meal a day plus a £25 weekly allowance).

openDays.text: Next Egham campus open day: Saturday 14 November 2026. Online open days: Wednesday 4 November and Wednesday 9 December 2026. No 2027 dates listed yet.

source.evidence: Our next Open Day will be taking place on Saturday 14 November.

contextual.summary: UK-resident applicants who meet the course entry requirements and Royal Holloway's widening access criteria automatically get a contextual offer of up to 2 A-level grades lower; there is no separate application.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to 2 A-level grades lower than the entry requirements advertised (subject-specific grades and GCSEs are not reduced; not for Integrated Foundation Year courses)

criteria.detail: In Local Authority care for more than 3 months at the time of applying: you automatically get a contextual offer if you meet all the course entry requirements (you may also be eligible for the £3,000-a-year bursary).
Disability or health condition that impacts your daily life (guided by the definitions on the UCAS form, which typically follow the Equality Act 2010).
Mature student (aged 21 or over when the course starts).
Estranged from parents.
Refugee or asylum seeker.
In receipt of free school meals.
Have caring responsibilities.

Attend an 'Aspiring School': the lowest 30% of colleges and lowest 20% of schools on pupils' performance in three academic qualifications (Gov.UK data); Royal Holloway publishes a list. Counts towards the 'meet 2 of these 3' route.
Home postcode in IMD quintile 1 or 2 (English indices of deprivation 2025, deciles 1 to 4). Counts towards the 'meet 2 of these 3' route.
Home postcode in a lower participation in higher education neighbourhood (POLAR4 quintile 1). Counts towards the 'meet 2 of these 3' route.

contextual.rulesText: You must be a UK resident and currently or previously at a UK school or college. Then either (1) you have been in Local Authority care for more than 3 months, or (2) you meet 1 of: disability or health condition, mature student, estranged from parents, refugee or asylum seeker, free school meals, caring responsibilities, or (3) you meet 2 of: attend an Aspiring School, IMD quintile 1/2 postcode, POLAR4 quintile 1 postcode. Nothing extra to do: Royal Holloway uses your UCAS form. minCriteria 2 applies to route (3) only.

contextual.summary: Home-fee UCAS applicants in the most disadvantaged group of UCAS's Multiple Equality Measure, or who are care experienced or seeking sanctuary, can get an offer up to 16 UCAS points (about two grades) lower.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to 16 UCAS Tariff points, or the equivalent of two grades, below the typical entry requirements for your chosen course.

criteria.detail: Group 1 of UCAS's Multiple Equality Measure 1 (MEM1) or Multiple Equality Measure 2 (MEM2). The MEM groups combine local-area higher-education participation (POLAR4), area deprivation (Index of Multiple Deprivation and Income Deprivation Affecting Children Index), the type of school you attend, free school meal eligibility and whether you attended an independent or state school. Group 1 is the students least likely to enter higher education.
Care experienced: spent any amount of time in care at any point in their life.
Seeking sanctuary: seeking asylum or granted refugee status by the UK government (international students are otherwise not eligible).

contextual.rulesText: No separate application: Salford uses the contextual data in your UCAS application. You must live in the UK, apply through UCAS for a full-time undergraduate course, be assessed as paying home fees and be studying three A levels, a BTEC Extended Diploma or a mix of A levels and BTEC (T Levels are not currently included). Meeting the criteria does not guarantee an offer. If you qualify for both a contextual and a Local Talent offer, the contextual offer takes precedence.

source.evidence: If you fall into Group 1 of either MEM1 or MEM2, you will be eligible for a contextual offer.

notes: Salford's offers are in UCAS Tariff points (104 points on every course recorded), not A-level grades, and it publishes no grade equivalent.

contextual.summary: Sheffield's Access Sheffield policies can give you a lower 'contextual offer' (shown as the 'Access Sheffield offer' on each course page) if you meet one or more criteria, such as living in a lower-participation area, free school meals or care experience.
contextual.typicalReduction: One, two or three grades below the standard A Level requirements (Access+ criteria and access programmes: up to two grades below)

criteria.detail: Live in a neighbourhood in IMD 2019 quintile 1 or 2 (check with Sheffield's Access+ postcode checker); assessed automatically from your UCAS application
Entitled to free school meals at some point in the six years before your final KS4 year (the year you were aged 15-16); checked automatically from the National Pupil Database
Care experienced (lived in public care or as a looked-after child at any stage up to age 18), or a care leaver recognised by your local authority
Young carer: responsible for providing unpaid care to someone with, for example, a long-term illness, disability, mental health condition or addiction
Estranged from your family: no relationship with, or support from, your parent(s) or carer(s) (for example no communication for 12 months and the situation is irreconcilable)
Forced migrant: asylum seeker, refugee or granted humanitarian protection
Parenting responsibilities: a parent of, or responsible for the care and wellbeing of, a child aged 17 or under

Took part in Access to Sheffield (Y12-13), the Access to Sheffield Summer School, Sheffield's Sutton Trust Summer School or the national Realising Opportunities programme: contextual offer up to two A Level grades below the standard entry requirements (the Access to Sheffield Summer School page says up to three)

Taking an EPQ on a topic relevant to your degree, Core Maths or Further Maths alongside three A Levels: contextual offer one A Level grade below the standard requirements, subject to a specific grade in that qualification (only on courses that list it)

contextual.rulesText: If you meet one or more of the Access Sheffield criteria you could get a contextual offer. You need home fee status (separate terms apply to forced migrants). For the Access+ criteria (area, free school meals, care, carer, estranged, parenting, forced migrant) Sheffield must also be your Firm choice with UCAS for the contextual offer to apply when results are released; for the Access to Sheffield (Y12-13) programme the offer applies whether Sheffield is your Firm or Insurance choice (except Medicine). Admissions decisions are not made on contextual data alone.

source.evidence: If you meet one or more of the Access Sheffield criteria set out below, you could get a contextual offer.

notes: All course facts are for September 2027 entry: Sheffield hasn't published 2028-entry course pages yet (the 2028 course URLs redirect to the general course list).

Sheffield has two main Economics degrees: Economics BSc (L101, AAB including A-level Maths) and Economics BA (L100, AAB with no A-level subject requirement but GCSE Maths grade 6). Years 1 and 2 share the same core modules.

Every course page shows a standard offer and an 'Access Sheffield offer' (the contextual offer). Sheffield's policy page says contextual offers are one, two or three grades below the standard requirements.

Sheffield also gives contextual offers (up to two A Level grades below) to people who complete the Sutton Trust Summer School at Sheffield, Realising Opportunities, Access to Sheffield (Y12-13) or the Access to Sheffield Summer School; these are recorded as alternative offers on every course.
Every course here has an optional placement year (four years in total) and an optional year abroad.

Joint courses are split between schools: for example Accounting and Financial Management and Economics spends half its time in the Management School and half in the School of Economics. The School of Economics is in the Elmfield Building, Northumberland Road, S10 2TU; the coordinates are for the University's main address.
The Access+ Travel Bursary helps eligible students with travel costs to open days and offer holder days.
Not added, to keep to 8 courses: Business Management BA (N200), Accounting and Financial Management BA (N420) and Financial Mathematics BSc.

source.evidence: Studio apartment, shared occupancy £5,847

contextual.summary: UK applicants with one or more widening-access indicators (such as a low-participation postcode, a school with low progression, a listed access programme, or care experience) are considered against lower 'Minimum' entry grades. It does not guarantee an offer.
contextual.typicalReduction: Each course page publishes lower 'Minimum' grades for widening access students, e.g. Economics A-levels ABB instead of AAA.

criteria.detail: Your home postcode is in the lowest 40% of the Scottish (SIMD) or English, Welsh or Northern Irish (IMD) deprivation indexes. ACORN data is also used.
You attend or most recently attended a school or college with low progression to higher education or low attainment, using school-level data for your nation.

You took part in a widening access programme: Sutton Trust Summer School, LEAPS, Focus West, Lift Off, Aspire North, Reach, Fife First Chances Programme or the Scottish Wider Access Programme (SWAP). The policy also mentions University of St Andrews outreach programmes and government-supported initiatives.
Care experienced or looked after, verified with evidence. Care-experienced applicants are also covered by the University's offer pledge.
Young carer or caring responsibilities, verified with evidence.
Estranged from family, verified with evidence.
Refugee, asylum seeker or displaced person, verified with evidence.
From a group known to be under-represented in higher education or known to have faced disadvantage (for example Gypsy, Traveller, Roma, Showman and Boater communities), subject to verification.

contextual.rulesText: Standard: applications where no contextual indicators have been identified. Minimum: applications where one or more contextual indicators have been identified. Contextual information is collated centrally for applicants with Home or rest-of-UK (RUK) fee status, and the University's online entry indicator shows which category applies. Contextual information alone does not result in an automatic offer. The University pledges an offer to first-degree applicants who declare a looked after or care experienced background (or who live in the most deprived 20% of Scotland and attend a school with lower than average progression), if they show they want to study the subject and meet the entry requirements at the first attempt.

source.evidence: Minimum: applications where one or more contextual indicators have been identified.

notes: St Andrews is in Scotland, so Honours degrees are four years. Both MA (Hons) and BSc (Hons) are undergraduate degrees; Economics has the same content either way.
Course pages show 'Standard' and 'Minimum' entry grades. Minimum applies to widening access students identified by the University's online entry indicator (see the contextual admissions page).
Taking part in the Sutton Trust Summer School counts as a widening access indicator, so those students are considered against the Minimum grades (recorded as an alternative offer on each course).
Joint degrees have no page of their own: the subject with the higher entry requirements sets the grades.
No admissions test for these courses; St Andrews is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry.
Gateway and Supported Pathways programmes are for Home Funded applicants in Scotland, so they are not recorded as options for students from England.
The 'academic entry explained' page lists 14 January as the application deadline for UK applicants (all courses except Medicine); the page does not say which entry year it applies to.

Economics BA (International Honours) with the College of William & Mary (two years at each) is listed, but its page says entry requirements 'have not been finalised', so it is not recorded as a course.

contextual.rulesText: Automatic contextual offers are for UK home students: the page says that where an applicant meets one or more of its criteria (POLAR4 quintile 1, IMD quintile 1, care experience, free school meals, estranged) the application is considered under contextual admissions, and you must still meet the standard admissions requirements. criteria.detail: Your home postcode on the UCAS application is in decile 1 or 2 of the Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD); Sussex makes the offer automatically.
Your home postcode on the UCAS application is in POLAR4 quintile 1; Sussex makes the offer automatically.
You received free school meals while attending secondary school. Sussex uses the free school meals information on your UCAS application (students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland).
You have been looked after in care for more than three months; tick the care-experienced box on the UCAS form.
You are an estranged student (studying without the support and approval of a family network); tell the admissions team when you apply.
You have refugee status or Humanitarian Protection; use the residential category on the UCAS form to show this.
You are a young carer (under 18, helping to look after a family member who is ill, disabled, has a mental health condition or misuses drugs or alcohol); tell the admissions team when you apply.
You are registered on the Sussex Inspires programme (Year 12) and meet Sussex's widening participation criteria; Sussex applies the contextual offer to all registered students who do.

You are a student at a partner college with a Progression Agreement (East Sussex College Group, Varndean College, Littlehampton Academy, Brighton Aldridge Community Academy, Thomas Bennett Community College); the contextual offer is automatic.

Sussex says it will still consider you for a contextual offer if you have faced other challenges that disrupted your education (for example disability, serious bereavement, long-term illness or homelessness).

Postcode (IMD or POLAR4) and free school meals are picked up automatically from your UCAS application; for care, estranged and young carer status you are encouraged to tell Sussex's admissions team. The exact reduction in grades varies depending on the course.

unis.name: Swansea University

settingEvidence.evidence: Swansea University spans two stunning campuses at each end of Swansea’s waterfront.

fees.text: £9,790 per year for UK (Home) students starting in September 2027 (2027/28), the same as the 2026/27 fee. Swansea says any future Welsh Government fee changes (such as inflation-linked rises) will be reflected in what it charges. A Year Abroad is charged at 15% and a Year in Industry at 20% of the standard fee.

livingCosts.text: University halls cost £130–£258 a week depending on the room (average £185 a week, about £7,400 for a 40-week contract, for a medium en-suite); utilities, internet and contents insurance are included and a £100 reservation deposit is payable (2026/27). A room in a private shared house averages about £122 a week rent plus about £16 a week bills.

contextual.summary: Access UCL gives UK-domiciled applicants from underrepresented groups a lower offer than the standard one (if UCL selects them for an offer); it is not a guaranteed offer.
contextual.typicalReduction: Lower than the standard offer; the exact grades are on each course page (for the courses recorded here, one to two grades lower, e.g. A*AA becomes A*AB for Economics and A*BB for Economics and Statistics).

criteria.detail: Live in a postcode in IMD Quintile 1 (decile 1 or 2) in the datasets UCL uses in the 2027 cycle, and attend(ed) a UK state school for the A levels (or equivalent) used for your offer. UCL has a postcode checker on its Access UCL page.
Live in a postcode in TUNDRA LSOA Quintile 1 in the datasets UCL uses in the 2027 cycle, and attend(ed) a UK state school for the A levels (or equivalent) used for your offer.

Received or been registered for UK government-funded Free School Meals at some point in the six years up to the end of Key Stage 4 (age 15-16), and attend(ed) a UK state school for your Level 3 qualifications. You must have been officially registered; UCL asks you to email it within two weeks of applying to confirm.
Estranged from both parents, with satisfactory evidence from a recognised third party.
Spent time in local authority care (care experienced), with satisfactory evidence from a recognised third party. You may also qualify if you attend(ed) a UK independent school.

contextual.rulesText: You may be eligible if you attend(ed) a UK state school for A levels or equivalent and one (or more) of these applies: you live in an eligible postcode; you were registered for Free School Meals in Key Stage 4 or below; you are estranged from your parents; you have spent time in local authority care. Access UCL is not a guaranteed offer scheme and eligibility does not mean you will get an offer. Most eligibility is picked up automatically from your UCAS application. UCL says the criteria are for the 2027 UCAS cycle only and may change for the 2028 cycle.

source.evidence: Access UCL is our contextual offer scheme for UK-domiciled undergraduate applicants from groups that are underrepresented at UCL.

notes: All six courses use 2027 entry: UCL's course pages show a September 2027 start and a 13 January 2027 UCAS equal-consideration deadline (UCL says applications may stay open after it). No 2028 option is shown yet.

UCL does not use UCAS tariff points: standard offers range from A*A*A to ABB depending on the course, and it asks for at least two A levels from its preferred list (which includes Geography and Psychology). General Studies, Critical Thinking and Global Perspectives and Research are not accepted, and the EPQ is not part of its standard entrance requirements (https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/undergraduate/how-apply/entry-requirements).
Economics (L100) and Economics with Study Abroad (L101) require the TMUA for 2027 entry (UCL's course page and UAT-UK's official list agree). No test is listed for the other courses recorded here.
Every course recorded here asks for an A* in A level Mathematics (Mathematics with Economics also needs Further Mathematics), so Mathematics A* is the key grade for UCL.

UCL runs an Open Day Travel Bursary for eligible Year 12 state-school students who live outside Greater London and meet widening participation criteria (applications were closed when checked; https://www.ucl.ac.uk/engage/widening-participation/get-involved/year-12-and-13/ucl-open-day-travel-bursary).

criteria.detail: If you live in England, UEA uses your postcode to check whether you live in an area of deprivation, measured with the Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD). Which IMD areas qualify isn't shown in the page text; use UEA's postcode eligibility checker on its 2027-entry page.
'Outreach Activity Participants' is one of UEA's contextual admissions schemes. The page text doesn't say which outreach activities count.

contextual.rulesText: You don't need to apply: UEA's admissions team works out your contextual offer automatically from data it and its partners already hold, if you live in England. UEA's schemes for 2027 entry are Nationwide Contextual Admissions, Outreach Activity Participants, Preparing for Medicine participants, Preparing for Pharmacy participants, Access to HE students and Medicine with a Gateway Year. All GCSE and subject requirements stay the same for contextual offers. contextual.summary: Home-fee applicants from UK state schools who meet one of three flags (free school meals, a deprived neighbourhood, or a below-average school), or who are care experienced, estranged or refugees, can get an offer of up to two grades lower; completing a listed access programme can also give a reduced offer.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to 2 A level grades lower than the standard offer (e.g. AAB rather than AAA), and/or an additional requirement such as an admissions test removed

criteria.detail: Individual Free School Meals flag: eligible for UK government-funded Free School Meals at some point in the past eight years (data comes from UCAS up to the end of Key Stage 4; for Key Stage 5 only, your school must confirm in writing).
Neighbourhood flag: lives in an area with a high level of deprivation (Index of Multiple Deprivation, 0-20%).
School flag: completed studies at schools/colleges where performance was below average and Free School Meals eligibility was higher than average.
Care experienced: a 'looked after child' for at least 3 months and eligible for Home fees (evidence needed; applicants from independent schools are also considered).
Estranged from both parents (under 25, studying without their support and approval) and eligible for Home fees (evidence needed).

UK-based, Home-fee applicants with humanitarian protection, refugee status or limited leave under the UKVI Afghan or Ukraine schemes, who studied A levels or equivalent in a UK school or college (evidence needed).

Successfully completed Realising Opportunities, Pathways to Law, Pathways to Banking and Finance or Pathways to Engineering (at Warwick or another university): considered for a reduced 'alternative' offer without meeting the flags above. Warwick Scholars Access participants are guaranteed an offer.

contextual.rulesText: State-school, Home-fee applicants who meet ONE of the three flags (free school meals, neighbourhood, school) are considered for a contextual offer. Care experienced, estranged and refugee applicants qualify without any other flag (the FAQ says independent-school applicants in these three groups are also considered). Undergraduate entry only (no foundation-year or graduate courses); eligibility does not guarantee an offer. Not currently counted: unpaid caring responsibilities, parenting responsibilities, armed forces connections, and disability or medical conditions (use the extenuating circumstances form instead). You do not have to make Warwick your firm choice.

notes: All course pages are for 2027/28 entry; no 2028-entry pages were published when checked (2026-10-17).
No admissions test (such as the TMUA) is listed for any of these courses.

Many York courses give an alternative offer up to one A-level grade lower for a good EPQ grade (the grade needed varies by course), and some for Core Maths or completing a free York online course (MOOC).

York gives an alternative Widening Participation offer (up to three grades below the standard offer) to students who complete Realising Opportunities, as well as its own Next Step York and Black Access programmes.

York's main undergraduate open days take place in June and July (post-16 outreach page).
York offers a guaranteed offer (or interview) to applicants living in Yorkshire, the Humber or Tees Valley who are on course to meet the entry requirements.
